steps.say: Welcome to the practice house! Some things here could start a fire. Can you find 10 of them?

lines.hz_pan: A pan handle sticking out. Turn handles in, so nobody knocks the pan.
lines.hz_candle: A candle near the curtains. Keep candles away from things that burn.
lines.hz_heater: A towel on the heater. Never put things on a heater.
lines.hz_plugs: Too many plugs in one socket. It can get too hot.
lines.hz_iron: An iron left on. Grown-ups switch it off and put it away.
lines.hz_matches: Matches on the table. Matches are for grown-ups: tell a grown-up if you find them.
lines.hz_lighter: A lighter on the sofa. Give it to a grown-up.
lines.hz_toaster: Paper next to the toaster. Keep paper away from hot things.
lines.hz_lamp: A cloth over a lamp. Lamps get hot.
lines.hz_alarm: The smoke alarm's light is off. Ask a grown-up to press its test button.
lines.hz_cooker_towel: A tea towel next to the cooker. Keep cloths away from the hob.
lines.hz_charger: A phone charging under a pillow. Charge things on a hard, open table.

steps.say: Find 10 things that could start a fire. Touch each one.
steps.done: You found 10 dangers! Now you know what to look for.

lines.hz_pan: A pan handle sticking out. Turn handles in.
lines.hz_plugs: Too many plugs in one socket.
lines.hz_matches: Matches on the table: for grown-ups.
lines.hz_lighter: A lighter on the sofa: give it to a grown-up.
lines.hz_cooker_towel: A tea towel by the cooker.
lines.hz_charger: A phone charging under a pillow.

steps.say: This time, find all 12 things that could start a fire.
steps.done: All 12! A real fire safety expert.

steps.say: Matches, lighters and candles are a grown-up's job. Never touch them: tell a grown-up. Touch Gus to tell him.
steps.done: Gus puts them away safely, up high.

steps.say: Now a fire drill! When the smoke alarm beeps, we get out. Listen: beep, beep.
The smoke alarm is beeping. What do you do?

choices.why: Never hide. Firefighters need to find you outside.

steps.say: Smoke rises up high. Get low, under the smoke.
steps.done: Low down, the air is clearer.

steps.say: Go to the front door, staying low.
Oh! Boxes block the front door. Use the other way out: the garden door.
Go to the garden door, staying low.
steps.done: Out of the house, the other way!

steps.say: You can stand up now. Go to the meeting point: the big tree.
steps.done: Everyone meets here, so the grown-ups know you are safe.

steps.say: Who calls {number}?

choices.text: A grown-up, from outside (or me, if no grown-up is there)

choices.why: Call from outside, where it is safe.

steps.say: Oh! Teddy is still inside. What do you do?

choices.why: Never go back in. Firefighters will help.

steps.done: Get out, stay out. That's the rule.

steps.say: Brilliant fire drill! Get low, get out, stay out, and call {number}.

check.say: The smoke alarm beeps. What do you do?
There is smoke in the room. Where is the air clearer?
Which one could start a fire?
Your toy is inside. You are outside. What now?

name_it.title: Get out, stay out
lines: The smoke alarm beeps: get out.
Call {number} from outside. Never go back in.
Matches, lighters and candles are a grown-up's job: tell one.
name_it.source: The fire services' advice (NFPA, the US Fire Administration, the UK fire and rescue services)

little.try_real: With a grown-up: find every smoke alarm at home and press its test button together. Choose your family's meeting point outside.

sources.fact: Matches, lighters and candles are for adults; children who find them should not touch them and should tell an adult.
sources.source: NFPA, children and fire; the UK fire and rescue services

sources.fact: Smoke alarms: test them every month; when one sounds, get out and stay out; meet at an outside meeting place; call the fire service from outside; never go back inside.
Get low and go under the smoke to your way out; have a meeting place outside.
sources.source: U.S. Fire Administration, home fire escape plans

sources.fact: Common causes of home fires: cooking left alone, candles near things that burn, heaters, overloaded sockets, matches and lighters children find.
sources.source: London Fire Brigade, safety in the home

middle.skill: Fire escape, and stop, drop and roll
middle.twist: The bedroom door is warm: you must use the other way out.
middle.can_now: get low, check a door with the back of the hand, close doors behind them, get out and call {number}, and stop, drop and roll

steps.say: The practice house. It's night, you are in bed, and the smoke alarm beeps. Let's practise getting out.
Beep, beep! What first?

choices.why: Never hide. Firefighters need to find you outside.
No time for toys or clothes. Get out.

steps.say: Get low, under the smoke.
steps.done: Low down, the air is clearer.

steps.say: Before you open a door, touch it with the back of your hand.
steps.done: It's cool. You can open it slowly.

steps.say: Open the door slowly and go through, staying low.
Close the door behind you. A closed door slows the fire and the smoke.
steps.done: Closed! That keeps the smoke back.

steps.say: Now to the front door, staying low.
Before you open a door, touch it with the back of your hand.
The door is warm. What do you do?

choices.why: A warm door can mean fire behind it. Use the other way.

steps.done: Leave it shut. The garden door is the other way.

steps.say: Check the garden door with the back of your hand.
Open the garden door and go through, staying low.
steps.done: Out of the house, the other way!

steps.say: Close the door behind you.
steps.done: Closed: it slows the fire and the smoke.

steps.say: You can stand up now. Go to the meeting point: the big tree.
Call {number} from outside. Here is a phone.
Press {number}: {number_words}.
steps.done: You called {number}. Say: fire, and your address.

steps.say: Oh! Teddy is still inside. What do you do?

choices.why: Never go back in. Firefighters will help.

steps.say: One more thing to know. If your clothes ever catch fire: stop, drop and roll. Let's practise.
Stop! Stand still: running makes flames bigger.
Drop to the ground.
Cover your face with your hands.
Roll over and over, until the flames are out.
steps.done: Stop, drop and roll! The flames are out.

steps.say: One more thing: a campfire, the safe way, with a grown-up. A camping trip in the practice garden!

not.under_tree: Not under the tree: sparks and flames can reach its branches.
not.by_tent: Not by the tent: it could catch fire.

steps.say: Where does the campfire go?
steps.done: In the ring of stones, on bare ground, far from the tent and the trees.

steps.say: Before it is lit: water ready, close by.
steps.done: A full bucket of water, ready.

steps.say: The grown-up lights it. How big should it be?

choices.text: Small: a few sticks at a time

choices.why: A small fire is easier to keep safe. And never leave it, never play with it.

steps.done: Small and cosy. Someone always watches it.

steps.say: Time to go: put it out. Drown it: pour water all over the ashes.
Stir the ashes with the little spade, so the water reaches every bit.
Feel for heat: hold the back of your hand near the ashes, not on them.
steps.done: Cool: it's out. Drown, stir, feel: too hot to touch is too hot to leave.

steps.say: You did the whole fire drill, and a safe campfire! Get low, get out, call {number}, never go back in. Drown, stir, feel.

check.say: The smoke alarm beeps at night. What do you do?
Before you open a door, you...

choices.text: Touch it with the back of your hand

check.say: The door is warm. What do you do?
Your clothes catch fire. What do you do?
When you are out, where do you go?

name_it.title: Fire escape
lines: Touch doors with the back of your hand: warm means use another way.
Clothes on fire: stop, drop and roll.
name_it.source: The fire services' advice (NFPA, the US Fire Administration, the UK fire and rescue services)

middle.try_real: With a grown-up: draw your home's escape plan, with two ways out of every room and your meeting point. Practise stop, drop and roll on a soft carpet.

sources.fact: A campfire: in a fire ring on bare ground, away from tents and overhanging branches, water ready, kept small, never left; put it out: drown it with water, stir, and feel for heat with the back of the hand: if it's too hot to touch, it's too hot to leave.
sources.source: US Forest Service, Smokey Bear, campfire safety

sources.fact: Feel a door with the back of your hand before opening it; if it is warm, use your second way out; close doors behind you.
Get low under smoke; go to your outside meeting place; call from outside; never go back inside.
sources.source: U.S. Fire Administration, home fire escape plans

sources.fact: If your clothes catch fire: stop, drop (to the ground), cover your face with your hands, and roll over and over until the fire is out.
Close doors at night and as you leave: a closed door holds back fire and smoke.
sources.source: London Fire Brigade, make an escape plan

big.twist: The bedroom door is warm, and the extinguisher's sweep must cover the whole fire.
big.can_now: escape a smoky house safely, and know when and how a fire extinguisher is used (Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep)

steps.say: The practice house again. First a quick escape, then the fire extinguisher. Grown-ups use extinguishers only on small fires.
The alarm beeps. Get low, under the smoke.
Check the door with the back of your hand.
Open it and go through, staying low.
Close it behind you.
To the front door, staying low.
Check the door with the back of your hand.
The door is warm. What now?

choices.text: Leave it shut and use the other way
Open it a little to look
choices.why: A warm door can mean fire behind it. Leave it shut.

steps.say: Out through the garden door, staying low.
Close it behind you.
Stand up and go to the meeting point.
Everyone is out. What now?

choices.text: Go back in for my phone
choices.why: Never go back in. Call from outside: a neighbour can lend a phone.

steps.done: Call {number} from outside. Never go back in.

steps.say: When may a grown-up use a fire extinguisher?

choices.text: On a small fire, with a way out behind them
On a big fire filling a room
choices.why: A big fire: get out, stay out, call {number}.

choices.text: When the way out is blocked by the fire
choices.why: Never let the fire get between you and the way out.

steps.done: Small fire, way out behind you. Otherwise: get out.

steps.say: Let's practise on this small fire in a metal bin. Stand with the way out behind you.
steps.done: Ready. The way out is behind you.

steps.say: P: Pull the pin.
A: Aim at the bottom of the fire.
S: Squeeze the handle.
S: Sweep from side to side, at the bottom of the fire.
S: Sweep from side to side, over the whole bottom of the fire.
Back away and keep watching it. Tell a grown-up, and call {number} if it was more than a tiny fire.
A fire is getting bigger. What do you do?

choices.why: If a fire grows, get out. Things can be replaced; people can't.

steps.say: Expert fire safety! Get low, check doors, get out, call {number}. Pull, aim, squeeze, sweep only for a small fire.

check.say: A door feels warm. What do you do?
What does PASS mean for a fire extinguisher?

choices.text: Pick it up and spray the ceiling

check.say: When should you not try to put a fire out?

choices.text: When it is big or spreading
Slows the fire and the smoke

name_it.title: Fire escape and the extinguisher
lines: Get low, check the door, close it behind you, get out.
A small fire only, with the way out behind you: Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep.
A big or growing fire: get out, stay out, call {number}.
name_it.source: NFPA, the US Fire Administration and OSHA (PASS)

big.try_real: With a grown-up: find out if your home has a fire extinguisher or a fire blanket, and where it is. Test the smoke alarms and plan two ways out of every room.

sources.fact: Use a portable extinguisher only on a small, contained fire, with your back to a clear way out; PASS: Pull the pin, Aim low at the base of the fire, Squeeze the handle, Sweep side to side; if in doubt, get out.
Feel doors with the back of the hand; a warm door: use the second way out; close doors behind you; never go back inside.
